name: What makes crown molding repair different from baseboard repair?

mainEntity.name: What makes crown molding repair different from baseboard repair?

acceptedAnswer.text: Crown molding repairs require working at ceiling height, making safety, ceiling alignment, and corner transitions major considerations. Ceiling and wall surfaces are rarely completely flat or square, especially in settling rooms, so crown repairs often demand compound miter cuts, coping joints, and backer blocks to achieve tight fits. Homeowners should clear floor space below the work area and move delicate furniture before work begins. For high or vaulted ceilings, specialized ladders or staging may be required to maintain safe, steady positioning.
acceptedAnswer.description: Crown molding involves ceiling-height work, compound angles, and coping joints to align with uneven walls, requiring specialized cutting and clear work areas below.
